note: Rejudged 2026-11-11 (independent judge) against rfc/full/rfc3032.txt Section 2.1 iv: "When an LSR would otherwise replace the label at the top of the stack with a new label, but the new label is "Implicit NULL", the LSR will pop the stack instead of doing the replacement." The six earlier units are byte-identical and still enforce item iv at the imposing sites (rsvpte transit pop, ingress empty push, bypass not stacked, fib-kernel empty push) and item v (TestLSPTableAllocateSkipsReservedLabels). The new positive tag on internal/plugins/fib/vpp/rfc3032_mplsentry_test.go::TestFibVPPLabelSwapProgramsBothStackPositions is wrong for this row: it swaps in-label 100 to ordinary out stacks {200} and {300,301} and asserts the S=1/S=0 split and stack order; label 3 never enters the body, so it says nothing about Implicit NULL or a pop and cannot go red if fib-vpp stopped popping. The unit in the same file that exercises item iv on VPP, TestFibVPPLabelPenultimatePop, is untagged: it asserts both S routes of an OpPop with a next hop carry exactly the single label 3 (implicitNullLabel) in uniform mode toward the IPv6 next hop (producer labelPath/swapOrPopStack, internal/plugins/fib/vpp/mpls.go). Fix owed: move the RFC3032-2.1-1 positive tag from the swap test to TestFibVPPLabelPenultimatePop, with a claim no wider than its body (fib-vpp sends label 3 as the out label, which VPP reads as pop; no running VPP proves the pop), and record its discrimination. Not covered: VPP's own reading of label 3 as a pop against a running VPP, the transit backup stack that empties to a pop, and TestMPLSIntegration_PushImplicitNull in the QEMU guest.
